segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning, Mr Tan. I'm Dr Liew, the anesthesiologist who'll be taking care of you during your knee surgery today. Can I start by confirming a few details?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, sure. Morning, doctor.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thanks. Let's start with your knee problem. How long have you been having issues with your left knee?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: About six months already, doc. Pain when I bend it or climb stairs. Tried physio and painkillers, but still got swelling and catching sensation inside.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, let's go through your medical history. I see in your records you're on montasone nasal spray and omeprazole. Can you confirm if you're still taking all these medications as listed?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Montasone spray, yes, one spray each nostril daily for my allergic rhinitis. But omeprazole? Oh, I stopped that in 2022 already. My GERD got better, so doctor said I can stop.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for clarifying that. So omeprazole was discontinued in 2022 after your GERD resolved?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, correct. No more heartburn since then, so no need for the pill anymore.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Excellent. Any allergies we should know about?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: None that I know of, doctor. Never had reactions to medicines or food.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Great. Have you eaten or drunk anything since midnight?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, nothing since last night dinner. Just a bit of water with my montasone spray this morning.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Any previous anesthesia experiences?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Once, when I had my appendix out in 2015. Went smoothly, no problems waking up or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Finally, how's your overall fitness? Can you walk, climb stairs, do daily activities?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can walk and climb stairs, but slowly because of the knee pain. Can't run or squat anymore, but otherwise okay lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you, Mr Tan. We'll be using general anesthesia with sevoflurane and vecuronium, plus a nerve block in your thigh to help with post-op pain. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No questions, doctor. Just want to get this knee fixed so I can play badminton again.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. We'll take good care of you. I'll see you in the operating room shortly.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:25] heart rate increased to one hundred twenty beats per minute, treated with intravenous metoprolol five milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling after the surgery? Let's start with your pain. On a scale from 0 to 10, how would you rate the pain in your left knee right now?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Eh, maybe around 3 or 4? It's sore, but the numbness from the block is still there, so it's not too bad.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good to hear. Any nausea or vomiting since waking up? Sometimes the anesthesia can make people feel queasy.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No nausea, thank goodness. But my nose feels a bit stuffy, like it's blocked up. Is that normal?

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That could be from the allergic rhinitis. We'll keep an eye on it, but it's not uncommon after anesthesia. Breathing comfortable otherwise?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, breathing's fine. No tightness or anything. Just the nose thing.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Any recollection of the operating room or waking up? Sometimes patients remember bits and pieces.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Nope, nothing at all. One minute I was talking to the anesthetist, next thing I know, I'm here. Like a magic trick!

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Glad to hear it was smooth. Any other concerns or questions before we get you mobilizing?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thanks for checking on me, doc.

claims.text: 22-year-old male undergoing elective arthroscopic partial meniscectomy of the left knee.
Reports left knee pain for six months, exacerbated by bending or stair climbing, with swelling and catching sensation despite physiotherapy and analgesics.
History of appendectomy in 2015 under general anesthesia without complications.
No ongoing respiratory symptoms; uses Montasone nasal spray for allergic rhinitis without current nasal issues. Relevant for airway management.
Functional status: able to walk and climb stairs slowly but cannot run or squat due to knee pain.
Current medication: Montasone nasal spray 1 spray each nostril daily for allergic rhinitis.
Omeprazole 20mg once daily was discontinued in 2022 after resolution of GERD.
No other current medications, including over-the-counter drugs or supplements.
No known drug allergies.
NPO from solids since midnight; consumed a small amount of water with Montasone nasal spray on the morning of surgery.
ASA-PS II: Patient has a mild systemic disease (musculoskeletal issue requiring surgery) without other systemic impairment.
Procedure: Arthroscopic partial meniscectomy of the left knee.
Anesthesia plan: General anesthesia with sevoflurane and vecuronium, supplemented with ultrasound-guided femoral nerve block for post-operative analgesia.
Propofol 120 milligrams administered at 08:00
